r: 词源: 源自拉丁语centum(百)，原指一美元的百分之一 → 分(货币单位)

c: Water freezes at zero degrees centigrade and boils at one hundred degrees at sea level.

r: 词根: centi-(百分之一) + metre(米，希腊语metron「度量」) → 一米的百分之一 → 厘米
c: Scientists measured the tiny fossil specimen with a precision ruler in millimetres and centimetres.
科学家用精密的尺子以毫米和厘米为单位测量这个微小的化石标本。

r: 词根: centr(中心，希腊语kentron「尖、中心」) + -al(形容词后缀) → 中心的
词根: centr(中心，希腊语kentron) + -e → 中心、中央
词根: cent(百，拉丁语centum) + -ury(名词后缀) → 一百年 → 世纪
c: The twentieth century witnessed remarkable advances in medicine, technology, and human rights.
二十世纪见证了医学、技术和人权方面的显著进步。

r: 词根: ceram(陶土，希腊语keramos「陶瓦」) + -ic(形容词后缀) → 用陶土烧制的 → 陶器的
c: The museum exhibition features ancient ceramic pottery from various civilizations around the world.
博物馆展览展出了来自世界各地不同文明的古代陶瓷陶器。

r: 词根: cere(谷物，拉丁语Ceres「谷物女神刻瑞斯」) + -al(名词/形容词后缀) → 谷物相关的食物 → 谷物
c: Many nutritionists recommend whole grain cereal as a healthy breakfast option for children and adults.

r: 词根: ceremon(仪式，拉丁语caerimonia「宗教仪式」) + -y(名词后缀) → 仪式
c: The graduation ceremony was held in the main auditorium with hundreds of students and their families.

r: 词根: cert(确定，拉丁语certus「确定的」，来自cernere「分辨」) + -ain(形容词后缀) → 确定的

c: In scientific research, absolute certainty is rare; conclusions are always subject to further evidence.
在科学研究中，绝对的确定性很少见；结论总是有待进一步证据验证。

r: 词根: certif(证明，拉丁语certificare「使确定」) + -ate(名词后缀) → 证明文件 → 证书
c: After completing the training program, participants received an official certificate of completion.

r: 词根: certif(证明) + -ic- + -ation(名词后缀) → 证明的行为或文件 → 证书
c: Professional certification can significantly enhance a person's career prospects and earning potential.
职业认证可以显著提升一个人的职业前景和收入潜力。

r: 词根: cert(确定，拉丁语certus) + -ify(动词后缀，使…) → 使确定、证明 → 证明
c: An independent auditor was hired to certify the company's financial statements for accuracy.
